products.architecture_notes: Parser architecture is clean. ZstDocument is a well-factored DTO. BUT: the product is incomplete — no writer, no compress/decompress capability. The class segregation is good for what exists; what's missing is a ZstWriter class.
required_refactors: Add ZstWriter class with compress/decompress methods

products.architecture_notes: Parser and writer well separated. CRITICAL: Multiple competing facades (models.py FodsDocument, spreadsheet_document.py, spreadsheet_model_document.py, Compat/FodsDocument). Compat/ and Spec/ are architecture stubs, not behavioral. The neutral model dict API coexists with class-based API — dual API problem (PQ-002). _shared/ base class not used.
required_refactors: Remove or archive spreadsheet_document.py and spreadsheet_model_document.py if redundant

products.architecture_notes: Better than FODS Python. neutral_model.py was healed from GOV_BLOCK (was 1916 LOC, now 279 LOC). Analytics distributed to fodt_document_edit.py, fodt_neutral_ops.py, text_document.py. Compat/ stubs are architecture markers.
Strong exception hierarchy (PbmError → 4 subtypes). PbmImage dataclass is clean. Parser doubles as entry point — acceptable for small format. Security guards (MAX_FILE_SIZE, MAX_DIMENSION) in parser.

UNUSUAL: set_cell_value(src, dest, row, col, value) is file-based — takes source and destination file paths, NOT a model object. This means edit operations mutate files, not in-memory models. This is a class segregation issue — edit responsibility lives in file I/O, not model layer.
required_refactors: Convert set_cell_value to model-based (take SylkDocument, return new SylkDocument)

products.architecture_notes: Read-only product. Codec does everything (parse, analyze, inspect). Dict-only model. No write architecture. This is minimal — appropriate if documented as POC but not as a product.
required_refactors: Add write_fodp() stub with NotImplementedError and descriptive message
